deed: Rita Levi-Montalcini discovered nerve growth factor and won the 1986 Nobel Prize in Medicine
title: Rita Levi-Montalcini: A Bedroom Laboratory under the Race Laws, Nerve Growth Factor and the Nobel Prize

trailer.text: Rita Levi-Montalcini, who was born in Turin, Italy, to a Jewish family, shared the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Stanley Cohen.
When Mussolini’s 1938 Race Laws forbade any non-Aryan from having a professional or academic career, she built a laboratory in her bedroom.
After the war, in the United States, she and Viktor Hamburger identified a substance in the tumour that they named nerve growth factor (NGF).
Her colleague, the biochemist Stanley Cohen, was able to isolate it from the tumour.
NGF was the first of many cell-growth factors that scientists found in animals.

paragraphs.text: Rita Levi-Montalcini was born in Turin, Italy, to a wealthy Jewish family.
According to JTA, she came from a family of Italian Jewish intellectuals.
She was raised by an authoritarian father.
He strongly disapproved of women’s education beyond finishing school.
She did not give up.
In eight months she completed years’ worth of Greek, Latin and mathematics.
She then entered medical school at the University of Turin.
According to an academic article published in PubMed Central, Rita Levi-Montalcini's father, Adamo Levi, was a talented engineer, and her mother, Adele Montalcini, was a gifted painter.

stations.title: The Race Laws, and a bedroom laboratory

paragraphs.text: She began her scientific career in danger, as a Jew in Fascist Italy.
Mussolini’s 1938 Race Laws forbade any non-Aryan from having a professional or academic career.
So she built a laboratory in her bedroom.
She made knives from sewing needles, and used an ophthalmologist’s scissors and a watchmaker’s forceps.
According to JTA, she begged farmers for eggs “for needy children” and extracted embryos from them for her work.
As Jews, she and Giuseppe Levi could not publish in Italian journals.
Their results were published in foreign journals in the early forties.
When the Germans invaded and started rounding up Jews, she and her family travelled south under false names.
According to JTA, the family opposed fascism.
According to Britannica, during the German occupation of Italy (1943–45) she was forced into hiding in Florence because of her Jewish ancestry.
Viktor Hamburger invited her to Washington University in St. Louis.
According to the Becker Center, she joined him as a research associate.
She and Hamburger found that many nerve cells die during normal development.
According to JWA, it was at Washington University that she first hypothesized the existence of a nerve growth factor.
She transplanted tumours onto the membrane around an embryo, and demonstrated that they could still encourage neural growth.
In 1952 she travelled to the Institute of Biophysics in Rio de Janeiro to learn the tissue-culture technique, in order to study the mysterious substance released by the tumour.
She and Hamburger named the substance they identified in the tumour "nerve growth factor" (NGF).
Cohen was able to isolate the NGF from the tumour.
According to an academic article published in PubMed Central, in 1947 Rita joined the laboratory of Viktor Hamburger in St. Louis, Missouri.
NGF was the first of many cell-growth factors that scientists found in animals.
According to Pietro Calissano, the discovery of the first growth factors was a breakthrough in the field of extracellular messengers.
The discovery deepened the understanding of deformities, senile dementia, delayed wound healing and tumour diseases.
According to JTA, her work with Cohen laid the foundations for research into cancer, Parkinson’s and ALS.
The 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Stanley Cohen and Rita Levi-Montalcini.
According to JWA, she won it on 13 October 1986.
Her Nobel Lecture was delivered on 8 December 1986 at Karolinska Institutet in Stockholm.
In the same year, she and Cohen were also awarded the Lasker Award for medical research.
She said that had she not been discriminated against and persecuted, she would not have received the Nobel Prize.
In 1987 she was awarded the US National Medal of Science.
The citation speaks of a breakthrough in neurobiology, in the discovery of nerve growth factor and its effect on the sympathetic nervous system.
In 1988 the English translation of her autobiography, In Praise of Imperfection, was published.
She was the first woman elected to the Pontifical Academy of Sciences in Rome.

stations.title: Rome, the Senate and the hundredth years

paragraphs.text: She founded the Institute of Cell Biology in Rome and served as its first director.
In 2002 she founded the European Brain Research Institute.
In 1992 she founded an education foundation.
According to an article in Blue Stocking Society, the foundation has supported more than 12,000 women and children.
In 1999 the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations named her one of the first four FAO Ambassadors in the fight against hunger.
In 2001 the President of Italy, Ciampi, appointed her senator for life.
This is one of Italy’s highest honours.
In 2006, at the age of 97, she held the deciding vote in the Italian parliament in a budget dispute.
She threatened to withdraw her support unless the government reversed its decision to cut science funding.
She died aged 103, the longest-living Nobel laureate.
The mayor of Rome said upon her death that it was a great loss "for all of humanity."
The matter of the drug Cronassial, made by the pharmaceutical company Fidia, drew criticism of her.

disagreements.question: When were the institute or the laboratory of cell biology in Rome founded?

versions.says: Britannica: in 1962 she established the Institute of Cell Biology in Rome
The Becker Center: in 1969 she established the Laboratory of Cell Biology of the National Research Council, and directed it until 1979

unknowns.text: Levi-Montalcini died on 30 December 2012 in Rome, Italy, aged 103, and became the longest-living Nobel Prize laureate.
Giuseppe Levi, her supervisor at medical school, was Jewish like her, and so they could not publish in Italian journals; their joint results were published in foreign journals in the early forties.

claims.text: פרס נובל לפיזיולוגיה או רפואה לשנת 1986 הוענק במשותף לסטנלי כהן ולריטה לוי-מונטלצ׳יני.
claims.quote: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1986 was awarded jointly to Stanley Cohen and Rita Levi-Montalcini

claims.text: לוי-מונטלצ׳יני נולדה בטורינו שבאיטליה למשפחה יהודית אמידה.
claims.quote: Rita Levi-Montalcini was born in Turin, Italy, to a wealthy Jewish family.

claims.text: חוקי הגזע של מוסוליני מ-1938 אסרו על מי שאינו ארי לעסוק בקריירה מקצועית או אקדמית.
claims.quote: when Mussolini’s newly published 1938 Race Laws forbade any non-Aryan from having a professional or academic career.

claims.text: היא בנתה מעבדה בחדר השינה, ויצרה סכינים מחטי תפירה והשתמשה במספריים של רופא עיניים ובפינצטה של שען.
claims.quote: She built a laboratory in her bedroom, fashioning scalpels from sewing needles, using an ophthalmologist’s tiny scissors and a watchmaker’s forceps.

claims.text: לוי-מונטלצ׳יני והמבורגר זיהו חומר בגידול שאותו כינו גורם גדילת העצב (NGF).
claims.quote: Levi-Montalcini and Hamburger figured out the cause: a substance in the tumour that they named nerve growth factor (NGF).

claims.text: הביוכימאי סטנלי כהן, עמיתה באוניברסיטת וושינגטון, הצליח לבודד את ה-NGF מהגידול.
claims.quote: From that point, biochemist Stanley Cohen, her colleague at Washington University, was able to isolate the NGF, a protein subunit, from the tumour.

claims.text: ה-NGF היה הראשון מבין גורמי גדילת תאים רבים שמדענים מצאו בבעלי חיים.
claims.quote: NGF was the first of many cell-growth factors scientists would find in animals.

claims.text: ב-2001 קיבלה את אחד מאותות הכבוד הגבוהים באיטליה כשהפכה לסנאטורית לכל החיים.
claims.quote: She received one of Italy’s highest honours in 2001 when she became a senator for life

claims.text: לוי-מונטלצ׳יני מתה בגיל 103 והפכה לזוכת הנובל שחיה הכי הרבה שנים.
claims.quote: Levi-Montalcini died aged 103 years, thereby becoming the longest-living Nobel Laureate.

claims.text: לפי JWA, באוניברסיטת וושינגטון ב-1951 העלתה לראשונה את ההשערה לקיומו של גורם גדילת העצב.
claims.quote: It was at Washington University, in 1951, that Levi-Montalcini first hypothesized the existence of the nerve growth factor.

claims.text: לפי JTA, היא באה ממשפחה של אינטלקטואלים יהודים איטלקים בטורינו.
claims.quote: comes from a family of Italian Jewish intellectuals in Turin.

claims.text: היא גדלה אצל אב סמכותני שהתנגד בתוקף להשכלת נשים מעבר לבית ספר לעידון.
claims.quote: Rita Levi-Montalcini was raised by an authoritarian father who strongly disapproved of women’s education beyond finishing school

claims.text: היא דחסה לשמונה חודשים שנים של לימודי יוונית, לטינית ומתמטיקה ואז נכנסה לבית הספר לרפואה באוניברסיטת טורינו.
claims.quote: she crammed years’ worth of Greek, Latin and mathematics into eight months, and then entered medical school at the University of Turin.

claims.text: לוי-מונטלצ׳יני החלה את הקריירה המדעית שלה בסכנה, כיהודייה באיטליה הפשיסטית.
claims.quote: Rita Levi-Montalcini began her scientific career in danger, as a Jew in Fascist Italy.

claims.text: לפי JTA, היא התחננה בפני חקלאים לביצים "לילדים נזקקים" והפיקה מהן עוברים לעבודתה.
claims.quote: She begged for eggs “for needy children” from farmers and extracted the embryos for her work.

claims.text: כיהודים, היא וג׳וזפה לוי לא יכלו לפרסם בכתבי עת איטלקיים, ותוצאותיהם פורסמו בכתבי עת זרים בראשית שנות הארבעים.
claims.quote: As Jews, they couldn’t publish in Italian journals, but their results were published in foreign journals in the early 1940s.

claims.text: כשהגרמנים פלשו והחלו לאסוף יהודים, היא ומשפחתה נסעו דרומה בשמות בדויים.
claims.quote: When the Germans invaded and started rounding up Jews, she and her family travelled south under false names.

claims.text: לפי JTA, הוריה היו אנשי משפחה אנטי-פשיסטית, ולכן חיו במחבוא בפירנצה בשם בדוי לוביזאטו.
claims.quote: they were forced to live clandestinely in Florence under the assumed name of Lovisato

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה, ב-1947 הזמין אותה ויקטור המבורגר להצטרף אליו באוניברסיטת וושינגטון.
claims.quote: In 1947 Victor Hamburger, then director of the zoology department at Washington University in St. Louis, invited Levi-Montalcini to join him.

claims.text: לפי נובל, המבורגר הזמין אותה לסנט לואיס ב-1946, והיא נשארה שם 30 שנה.
claims.quote: Her future was secured in 1946, when Viktor Hamburger himself, curious about their conflicting results, invited her to the Washington University in St. Louis, Missouri.

claims.text: לפי מרכז בקר, בספטמבר 1947 קיבלה את הזמנת המבורגר לשתף פעולה כחוקרת עמיתה.
claims.quote: In September 1947 Rita Levi-Montalcini accepted Hamburger’s invitation to collaborate with him as a research associate.

claims.text: היא והמבורגר גילו שתאי עצב רבים מתים בהתפתחות רגילה.
claims.quote: Together, they found that many nerve cells die during normal development, and that limb amputations heighten this loss.

claims.text: היא השתילה גידולים על הקרום סביב עובר והוכיחה שהם עדיין מעודדים צמיחת עצבים.
claims.quote: Levi-Montalcini transplanted tumors onto the membrane around an embryo, where they were only connected to the developing animal by a common blood supply, and demonstrated that the tumors could still encourage neural growth.

claims.text: ב-1952 הצליחה לבודד חומר שנלקח מגידולים בעכברים וגרם לצמיחה נמרצת של מערכת העצבים בעוברי תרנגולת.
claims.quote: In 1952 she succeeded in isolating a substance harvested from tumors in mice that caused vigorous nervous system growth in chicken embryos.

claims.text: לפי פייטרו קליסאנו, גילוי גורמי הגדילה הראשונים היה פריצת דרך בתחום המסרים החוץ-תאיים.
claims.quote: The discovery of these first growth factors was a “breakthrough in the field of extracellular messengers,”

claims.text: גילוי גורמי הגדילה העמיק את ההבנה של בעיות רפואיות כמו מומים, שיטיון סנילי, ריפוי איטי של פצעים ומחלות גידול.
claims.quote: The discovery of what are now known as growth factors has provided a deeper understanding of medical problems like deformities, senile dementia, delayed wound healing, and tumor diseases.

claims.text: לפי JTA, העבודה של לוי-מונטלצ׳יני וכהן הניחה יסודות למחקר בסרטן, פרקינסון ו-ALS.
claims.quote: laid the foundations for research into cancer, Parkinson’s, and ALS.

claims.text: לפי JWA, היא זכתה בנובל ב-13 באוקטובר 1986.
claims.quote: Rita Levi-Montalcini’s pioneering work on nerve growth earned her the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine on October 13, 1986.

claims.text: הרצאת הנובל שלה נישאה ב-8 בדצמבר 1986 במכון קרולינסקה בשטוקהולם.
claims.quote: Rita Levi-Montalcini held her Nobel Lecture on 8 December 1986, at Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm.

claims.text: ב-1986 הוענק לה ולכהן פרס לסקר למחקר רפואי.
claims.quote: In 1986, she and Cohen were awarded the Albert Lasker Medical Research Award.

claims.text: לוי-מונטלצ׳יני אמרה שאילולא הופלתה לרעה או נרדפה, לא הייתה מקבלת את פרס נובל.
claims.quote: If I had not been discriminated against or had not suffered persecution, I would never have received the Nobel Prize.

claims.text: ב-1987 הוענק לה מדל המדע הלאומי של ארה״ב, וב-1988 פורסמה האוטוביוגרפיה שלה.
claims.quote: In 1987 she was awarded the National Medal of Science, and an autobiographical work, In Praise of Imperfection, was published in 1988.

claims.text: ציטוט מדל המדע הלאומי: פריצת דרך בנוירוביולוגיה בגילוי גורם גדילת העצב והשפעתו על המערכת העצבית הסימפתטית.
claims.quote: For a major breakthrough in neurobiology by her discovery of the Nerve Growth Factor and its effect on the growth of the sympathetic nervous system

claims.text: היא הייתה האישה הראשונה שנבחרה לאקדמיה האפיפיורית למדעים ברומא.
claims.quote: She also became the first woman ever named to membership in the Pontifical Academy of Sciences in Rome.

claims.text: היא ייסדה את המכון לביולוגיה של התא ברומא וכיהנה כמנהלת הראשונה שלו, וייסדה ב-2002 את המכון האירופי לחקר המוח.
claims.quote: she founded and was the first director of the Institute of Cell Biology in Rome. She founded the European Brain Research Institute in 2002.

claims.text: היא ייסדה ב-1992 קרן חינוך, ולפי המאמר הקרן תמכה ביותר מ-12,000 נשים וילדים.
claims.quote: to this day her charity has supported more than 12,000 women and children.

claims.text: ב-1999 מינה אותה ארגון המזון והחקלאות של האו״ם לאחד מארבעת שגרירי ה-FAO הראשונים במאבק ברעב.
claims.quote: In 1999, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations named Rita Levi-Montalcini one of its first four FAO Ambassadors

claims.text: ב-2006, בגיל 97, הייתה לה ההצבעה המכרעת בפרלמנט האיטלקי במחלוקת תקציב.
claims.quote: In 2006, at the age of 97, she held the deciding vote in the Italian parliament in a budget dispute.

claims.text: היא איימה למשוך את תמיכתה אלא אם הממשלה תבטל את ההחלטה לקצץ במימון המדע.
claims.quote: She threatened to withdraw her support unless the government reversed its decision to cut science funding.

claims.text: לפי מקורות אחרים, נולדה למשפחה יהודית ספרדית בטורינו.
claims.quote: Levi-Montalcini was born in 1909 to a Sephardic Jewish family in Turin, Italy.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, היא נשארה באוניברסיטה עשרים ושש שנים.
claims.quote: offered her a post as lecturer at the university, where she remained for twenty-six years, continuing

claims.text: לפי JTA, עבודת הנובל נבעה מעבודה שהושלמה בארה״ב ב-1951, גילוי ה-NGF.
claims.quote: Her Nobel Prize stemmed from work completed in the U.S. in 1951: discovery of NGF, a protein growth factor that stimulates nerve cell development.

claims.text: לפי JTA, היא הייתה האישה הראשונה באקדמיה האפיפיורית ב-1968 האישה השישית באקדמיה האמריקאית למדעים.
claims.quote: in 1968, the sixth woman to gain admittance to the American Academy of Science.

claims.text: לפי מרכז בקר, ב-1975 הייתה האישה הראשונה שהותקנה באקדמיה המדעית האפיפיורית.
claims.quote: In 1975 Levi-Montalcini became the first woman to be installed in the Pontifical Scientific Academy.

claims.text: לפי בריטניקה, ב-1962 הקימה את המכון לביולוגיה של התא ברומא.
claims.quote: Levi-Montalcini established the Institute of Cell Biology in Rome in 1962

claims.text: לפי מרכז בקר, ב-1969 הקימה את מעבדת הביולוגיה של התא של המועצה הלאומית למחקר ברומא וניהלה אותה עד 1979.
claims.quote: In 1969 she established the Laboratory of Cell Biology of the Italian National Research Council in Rome, serving as its director until 1979

claims.text: לפי מאמר אקדמי שפורסם ב-PubMed Central, אביה של ריטה לוי-מונטלצ׳יני, אדמו לוי, היה מהנדס מוכשר, ואמה, אדלה מונטלצ׳יני, הייתה ציירת מחוננת.
claims.quote: Her father, Adamo Levi, was a talented engineer, and her mother, Adele Montalcini, a gifted painter.

claims.text: לפי מאמר אקדמי שפורסם ב-PubMed Central, ב-1947 הצטרפה ריטה למעבדתו של ויקטור המבורגר בסנט לואיס שבמיזורי.
claims.quote: In 1947, Rita joined the laboratory of Viktor Hamburger in St. Louis, MO.

claims.text: ב-2001 מינה אותה נשיא איטליה צ׳אמפי לסנאטורית לכל החיים.
claims.quote: Dal primo agosto 2001 era senatrice a vita, nominata da Carlo Azeglio Ciampi

claims.quote: Rome Mayor Gianni Alemanno, announcing her death in a statement, called it a great loss "for all of humanity."
